product: Lithology geochemistry of Olson and Hawkins (2014; workbooks Lith-Nutrient and Lith-MajorOxides) applied to the lithologies and ranks of the Geologic Map of Alaska (SIM 3340)
citation: Olson and Hawkins 2014, Geochemical characteristics of the conterminous United States, USGS data release doi:10.5066/F7X0653P (method: Olson and Hawkins 2012, Water Resources Research 48:W02504); Wilson et al. 2015, USGS SIM 3340, doi:10.3133/sim3340

uncertainty_method: Monte Carlo (default 1000 draws): class value shifted by sdlog/sqrt(n records), shared across units; formation deviation lognormal with SD formation_sd x sdlog (mean-preserving); lithology shares drawn within the SIM 3340 rank ranges (major >=33%, minor 10-33%, incidental <10%, indeterminate 10-100%); classes with fewer than min_n records get the 90th percentile sdlog of well-sampled classes
assumptions: CONUS class values represent Alaskan rocks of the same name; SIM 3340 terms match the CONUS lithology vocabulary (unmatched terms are reported); within-class spread among records is formation-to-formation variation (formation_sd = 1, conservative); modifiers assigned by hand from unit descriptions; surficial deposits as mapped
extent: Alaska (SIM 3340 map); class values from CONUS
access: automatic (download once: SIM 3340 geodatabase and two workbooks)
